title: UAE Logistics Brief
lede: Iran now says the Strait of Hormuz is completely closed to ships that do not follow its rules, after the worst month on record for attacks on shipping. Saudi air links are still mostly down while European airlines return to Dubai, so road into KSA stays our main lane and Europe belly space into the UAE is opening up.

stories.headline: Iran declares Hormuz "completely closed" as talks open in Tehran
body: On the evening of 26 October, Iran's armed forces chief of staff said Tehran has full control of the strait and that it is completely closed. Ships may pass only if they follow Iranian rules. Foreign Minister Araghchi said the strait's routes and management "will not be the same as they once were".

On the same day, Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan held talks with Iran in Tehran to open negotiating channels. Brent eased to $115.15 on 27 October. Britain and France are planning a mine-clearing mission for Hormuz, but only once fighting stops. CNN reports US forces could act against Iran within 96 hours of an order; no decision has been made.
stories.soWhat: New since yesterday: a formal closure claim and the first diplomatic channel. Keep pricing Gulf inbound sea on war terms and do not promise customers a reopening date.

stories.headline: October is the worst month on record for attacks on Gulf shipping
body: The Washington Institute counts 28 confirmed or reported attacks in and near the Strait of Hormuz in October, and 113 since 28 February. A Reuters review says more than 30 supertankers have been damaged, 11 of them this month.
Marisks recorded 12 ships attacked between 5 and 11 October, the highest weekly total of the war.
stories.soWhat: War-risk cover and carrier surcharges will not fall soon. Keep sea surcharges indexed, not fixed.

stories.headline: Khor Fakkan volumes up about 700% as Gulftainer doubles capacity
body: Weekly volume at Khor Fakkan has jumped from about 8,000 to 65,000 TEU as trade moves to ports outside Hormuz. Gulftainer is spending $2 billion to double capacity to 10 million TEU a year; phase one takes it to 5 million.
Inland, the Sajaa bonded dry port and a 150-hectare hub at Al Dhaid back up the port. A cited study puts overland rerouting at 2.4 to 4.2 times the cost per ton-km of sea.
stories.soWhat: East-coast inbound is now a volume lane, not a stopgap. Price drayage from Khor Fakkan to Dubai and Sajaa as a standing product.

stories.headline: Saudi skies still mostly shut despite Riyadh reopening
body: Cirium data show 45.1% of scheduled Saudi departures were cancelled or not flown between 8 and 25 October: 7,802 of 17,299. At Riyadh the figure was 86%. King Khalid airport reopened on 25 October, but most departures were still cancelled.

On 26 October the coalition intercepted a Houthi missile aimed at Riyadh; the Houthis say they targeted the airport. flydubai's Riyadh, Dammam and Abha suspension runs to 29 October, Etihad's to 5 November, and Air Arabia has no date.
stories.soWhat: New: hard numbers and a fresh attack on Riyadh. Restart dates may slip again, so keep road into KSA as the default and do not promise air transit times.

stories.headline: European airlines return to Dubai
body: Lufthansa restarted Dubai–Munich on 25 October and Dubai–Frankfurt on 26 October. SWISS returns to Zurich on 27 October, Eurowings on 1 November, British Airways on 4 November and Austrian on 12 December.
Gulf News says up to 36 weekly Dubai–Europe flights are due back between late October and December.
stories.soWhat: More belly space from Europe into Dubai. Expect Europe–UAE air rates to soften first; check our buy rates before peak contracts are fixed.

stories.headline: UAE warehouse tenants stay put as demand moves north and east
body: Warehouse lease renewals rose 21.6% to a record of about 8,200 in the first half, while new contracts fell 51.8% year on year (Cavendish Maxwell). CBRE puts Dubai industrial rent growth at about 12.3%.
The Northern Emirates opened more than 10 million sq ft of space in the first half, 5.2 million of it in Umm Al Quwain, and rents there fell 18.5% year on year.
stories.soWhat: Cheaper space is opening north and east. Price contract logistics bids from UAQ and Sharjah sites where the lane allows.

stories.headline: Dubai Mall readies a one-hour delivery app
body: A Dubai Mall Online app is coming that will deliver orders from the mall's stores within an hour, according to billboards in the mall and Downtown Dubai. No launch date has been given, and it is not yet known who will run delivery.
stories.soWhat: A same-hour retail delivery contract may go out soon. Sales should ask Emaar who is bidding.

stories.headline: Saudi Arabia seeks developers for Jeddah's 2.4m sqm Al Khumrah logistics zone
body: Mawani has opened expressions of interest for private firms to develop and run the Al Khumrah logistics zone. Submissions close on 20 November. A SAR 689 million, 17 km freight corridor linking it to Jeddah Islamic Port is due by end-2028.
Jeddah industrial and logistics occupancy stayed above 90% in the second quarter, with rents up 4.8% (JLL).
stories.soWhat: Jeddah is the Red Sea gateway our road lanes feed. Worth a look by contract logistics before 20 November.

competitors.name: DP World
competitors.headline: Plans Fujairah terminals to sit beside Jebel Ali; 500,000 TEU moved overland
body: DP World has an in-principle 50-year concession for two Fujairah sites. Al Rugaylat is planned for 2.5 million TEU, 1.7 million tonnes of general cargo and 190,000 car units a year; Dibba for 3.6 million tonnes. Construction has not started. It says the terminals could cut three to five days off some Indian Ocean services.
It has moved more than 500,000 TEU overland through its GCC network since March, and ran about 3,000 truck movements a day in August after adding 700 trucks.
competitors.soWhat: DP World is building an end-to-end east-coast-to-Jafza offer with its own trucks. Our freight team needs a drayage and clearance bundle that competes on price and speed.

competitors.name: FedEx
competitors.headline: Dubai hub wins IATA CEIV Pharma certification
body: FedEx's Dubai World Central hub, 57,000 sq m with 170 sq m of temperature-controlled storage, has IATA CEIV Pharma certification. FedEx now holds 30 such certifications worldwide.
New since our 26 October item: together with its GCC dangerous-goods road launch, FedEx now has a certified healthcare offer by air and road out of DWC.
competitors.soWhat: FedEx is building a full healthcare pitch in the UAE. Check our pharma certifications and cold-chain capacity before our healthcare renewals.

competitors.name: Aramex (baseline)
competitors.headline: Latest result: record Q2 revenue of Dh1.83 billion
body: Revenue rose 22% to Dh1.83 billion in Q2 2026, the highest in our history. Net profit was Dh47 million, about seven times a year earlier, and the EBITDA margin rose to 9.9% from 7%.
Freight forwarding had its best quarter, domestic express kept growing and international express volumes stabilised. Q3 results are not yet out.
competitors.soWhat: Freight and domestic carried the quarter. Protect those margins as KSA air returns and east-coast costs rise.

opportunities.title: Road into KSA, longer than planned
opportunities.text: 45% of Saudi flights were cancelled in the past three weeks, and Riyadh was targeted again on 26 October. Road express and FTL demand into KSA should hold into November.

opportunities.title: East-coast drayage as a product
opportunities.text: Khor Fakkan handles about 65,000 TEU a week. Shippers need regular trucking and clearance from there to Dubai and Sajaa.

opportunities.title: Cheaper Europe air buy
opportunities.text: Lufthansa, SWISS, Eurowings and BA are returning to Dubai. More belly space should lower our Europe–UAE buy rates.

opportunities.title: Northern Emirates warehousing
opportunities.text: Rents there are down 18.5% while Dubai's rise 12.3%. Room to bid contract logistics at lower cost.

opportunities.title: Same-hour retail delivery
opportunities.text: Dubai Mall's one-hour app will need a delivery partner.

watchouts.title: Hormuz closure claim
watchouts.text: Iran says only ships following its rules may pass. Expect more delays and higher war-risk costs on Gulf inbound sea.

watchouts.title: US strike window
watchouts.text: CNN says US forces could act within 96 hours of an order. Escalation would hit UAE air and sea again.

watchouts.title: Saudi restart dates may slip
watchouts.text: Houthi missiles keep targeting Riyadh. flydubai's 30 October return and Etihad's suspension to 5 November could both be extended.

watchouts.title: DP World land bridge
watchouts.text: Its own trucks and Fujairah plans compete directly with our freight and road products.

watchouts.title: UPS results today
watchouts.text: UPS reports Q3 on 27 October. Watch for Middle East surcharge and peak pricing comments.

watchouts.title: Fuel prices for November
watchouts.text: UAE announces November petrol and diesel prices around 31 October, with Brent near $115.

moves.title: Extend KSA road contracts to end-November
moves.text: Offer road shippers rates to 30 November, since Saudi air restarts keep slipping.

moves.title: Launch a Khor Fakkan drayage and clearance bundle
moves.text: One price for port pickup, customs and delivery to Dubai, Jafza or Sajaa, to answer DP World's trucking offer.

moves.title: Re-tender Europe–UAE air buy rates
moves.text: Ask carriers for new rates as European belly space returns from 25 October to 4 November.

moves.title: Prepare a November diesel surcharge update
moves.text: Be ready to move road surcharges the day UAE fuel prices come out, around 31 October.

moves.title: Check our pharma certification gap against FedEx
moves.text: List our CEIV Pharma and cold-chain sites and brief healthcare accounts before FedEx does.

moves.title: Bid from Northern Emirates warehouse space
moves.text: Cost new contract logistics bids on UAQ or Sharjah sites where the customer's lanes allow.

moves.title: Approach Emaar on Dubai Mall one-hour delivery
moves.text: Find out who runs delivery for the new app and pitch our same-day network.
